claims.claim: A WKE link gives a self-contained one-vertex reduction.
claims.evidence: Let (M,Q) witness that H=G[N(v)] is WKE. The triangles S={vxy:xy∈M} are edge-disjoint because M is a matching. For X=M∪{vq:q∈Q}, |X|=|M|+|Q|≤2|S|. Every triangle through v is hit by X: its link edge is either in M or, being in H−M, has an endpoint in Q. With G'=(G−X)−v, S is edge-disjoint from every packing in G' because its non-v edges lie in M⊆X. Thus ν(G)≥|M|+ν(G'), while X united with a transversal of G' gives τ(G)≤|X|+τ(G'). Consequently τ(G')≤2ν(G') implies τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.search_method: Direct definition-level proof with the empty-matching and residual cases included

claims.claim: Every graph whose every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link satisfies τ≤2ν.
claims.evidence: Induct on the number of vertices. Apply claim 0 at a guaranteed vertex v. The residual G' is a proper subgraph. Every nonempty subgraph of G' is also a subgraph of G, and the hypothesis concerns links inside each such subgraph, so the hypothesis is inherited without a quantifier change. Induction proves the inequality for G', and the WKE reduction transfers it to G.
claims.search_method: Inductive proof with explicit hereditary-quantifier audit

claims.claim: Every locally bipartite graph satisfies τ≤2ν.
claims.evidence: For every subgraph J⊆G and v∈V(J), J[N_J(v)] is a subgraph of the bipartite graph G[N_G(v)], hence is bipartite. By König's theorem, a bipartite link has a matching M and vertex cover Q with |Q|=|M|, which is a WKE witness since Q also covers the link after M is deleted. Thus every nonempty subgraph has a vertex with WKE link, and claim 1 applies.
claims.search_method: Hereditary link analysis followed by the matching-cover equality for bipartite graphs

claims.claim: Every triangle-free graph on at most eight vertices is WKE.
claims.evidence: The checker generated labelled triangle-free graphs recursively: a new labelled vertex was joined to each independent subset of the existing graph. This is exhaustive and duplication-free because deleting the newest vertex gives the unique parent, and its neighborhood is independent exactly when no new triangle is formed. For each Q, the complete WKE test used the equivalence that all edges induced by R=V−Q must form a matching forced into M and must extend to a matching of size at least |Q|; every returned (M,Q) was then checked literally against the WKE definition. Counts of generated graphs and validated witnesses agreed at every order 0–8, culminating in 4,682,270 of each at order eight. The checker exited with PASS using integer bit masks only.
claims.search_method: Exact exhaustive labelled-graph generation and complete matching/cover enumeration
claims.witness: A literal WKE pair (M,Q) was constructed and validated for every one of the 4,682,270 labelled order-eight triangle-free graphs and for every generated smaller graph.

claims.claim: The order-eight WKE bound is sharp: a triangle-free non-WKE graph exists on nine vertices.
claims.evidence: Take independent cyclic parts A0={0}, A1={1,2}, A2={3,4}, A3={5,6}, A4={7,8}, with all edges between consecutive parts. This graph is triangle-free. Any vertex subset inducing maximum degree at most one has order at most four: if it contains both vertices of a two-vertex part, both adjacent parts must be empty and the remaining two parts contribute at most two; if it contains at most one vertex per part, selecting five induces C5. In any WKE witness, |M|≤4 and hence R=V−Q has at least five vertices, while every edge of H[R] must lie in M, forcing H[R] to have maximum degree at most one—a contradiction. Independently, the checker found the maximum such R has order four and rejected all 33,701 eligible (M,Q) pairs across all 275 matchings.
claims.search_method: Concrete construction, exact subset analysis, and exhaustive direct WKE-witness rejection

claims.claim: Deleting every edge that lies in no triangle preserves both ν and τ.
claims.evidence: The triangle-edge subgraph G△ has exactly the same triangle family as G: every G-triangle retains all three edges, and every G△-triangle is already a G-triangle. Hence the feasible triangle packings are identical. Edges outside G△ occur in no triangle and cannot help hit one, so every transversal can discard them without loss. Therefore both optima are unchanged.

claims.claim: Triangle packing and covering are additive over triangle edge-overlap components.
claims.evidence: Distinct edge-overlap classes have disjoint edge supports; otherwise triangles containing a common support edge would lie in the same class. Packings from the classes can therefore be united without an edge conflict, and every global packing restricts to packings in the classes, proving ν=Σν_i. Likewise, unions of component transversals cover all triangles, while every global transversal restricts to a transversal of each class; disjoint support edge sets give τ=Στ_i. Edges in no triangle contribute zero.
claims.search_method: Two-sided optimization proof over disjoint triangle-edge supports

claims.claim: If the triangle-edge subgraph G△ is K4-free and 8-degenerate, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.evidence: Every nonempty subgraph J of the 8-degenerate graph G△ has a vertex v of J-degree at most eight. Since J is K4-free, its link at v is triangle-free: a link triangle together with v would form K4. Claim 3 makes this at-most-eight-vertex link WKE. Thus G△ meets claim 1's hereditary elimination hypothesis, so τ(G△)≤2ν(G△); claim 5 transfers the inequality to G.
claims.search_method: Degeneracy elimination with all subgraphs and link sizes checked explicitly

claims.claim: If G△ is K4-free and mad(G△)<9, then τ(G)≤2ν(G).
claims.evidence: Every nonempty subgraph of G△ has average degree below nine. If all its degrees were at least nine, its average degree would be at least nine, so it has an integer degree at most eight. Hence G△ is 8-degenerate. Together with the stated K4-freeness, claim 7 applies.
claims.search_method: Exact average-degree-to-degeneracy implication followed by claim 7

claims.claim: A subgraph-minimal K4-free counterexample would have every edge in a triangle and minimum degree at least nine.
claims.evidence: An edge in no triangle could be deleted without changing ν or τ by claim 5, leaving a proper K4-free counterexample and contradicting subgraph minimality. If d(v)≤8, K4-freeness makes G[N(v)] triangle-free, and claim 3 makes that link WKE. Claim 0 reduces the inequality to a proper subgraph, which satisfies it by minimality, again contradicting that G is a counterexample. Therefore every edge is triangular and δ(G)≥9.
claims.search_method: Minimal-counterexample audit under edge deletion and WKE vertex reduction

claims.claim: The inequality holds componentwise whenever every triangle edge-overlap component has either a locally bipartite structure or a K4-free 8-degenerate structure.
claims.evidence: For each triangle edge-overlap component, apply claim 2 if its support graph is locally bipartite and claim 7 if its support graph is K4-free and 8-degenerate. Every support edge belongs to a component triangle, so the support graph is its own triangle-edge subgraph. Claim 6 then sums the component inequalities, and claim 5 disposes of all edges outside the triangle supports.
claims.search_method: Componentwise case split followed by exact additivity

target_evidence: The exact target demands either τ(G)≤2ν(G) for every finite simple graph or an explicit graph with τ(G)>2ν(G). The draft establishes neither: its principal theorems retain local-bipartiteness or K4-free degeneracy hypotheses, and the nine-vertex construction is only non-WKE, not a counterexample to Tuza's inequality. The final writeup expressly acknowledges both limitations, so it does not overclaim target coverage. The verified infinite graph classes, exact WKE threshold, component decomposition, and necessary conditions for a minimal K4-free counterexample are nevertheless material progress. Therefore target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
